f: A.F. Harrold is an English poet who writes and performs for adults and children. He spends his time showing off onstage, writing poems and books, and stroking his beard (it helps churn the ideas). He is the author of The Book of Not Entirely Useful Advice , illustrated by Mini Grey; The Song from Somewhere Else , illustrated by Levi Pinfold; the Fizzlebert Stump series, illustrated by Sarah Horne; the Greta Zargo duology, illustrated by Joe Todd-Stanton, and the CILIP Carnegie and Kate Greenaway Medal-longlisted The Imaginary and The Afterwards , both illustrated by Emily Gravett. He is the anthologist of many poetry collections, including Midnight Feasts . He lives in Reading with a stand-up comedian and two cats. Speaker | 2023 | NLF Reading Challenge

b: Aashti Mudnani is a professional hunter of children’s books, illustration lover, listener of stories and chai drinker. She started Lightroom, a bookstore for children’s books when she was unable to find books she was…
f: Aashti Mudnani is a professional hunter of children’s books, illustration lover, listener of stories and chai drinker. She started Lightroom, a bookstore for children’s books when she was unable to find books she was looking for, for her own children. Seven years after the first idea and with the help of a whole lot of people, the store opened in 2013. She loves being outdoors, especially where there are more wild things than cityscapes. Delegate | 2023

b: Adam Gidwitz is the author of Max in the House of Spies, the Newbery Honor book The Inquisitor’s Tale, the New York Times bestseller A Tale Dark & Grimm and its companions, the bestselling Unicorn Rescue Society series,…
f: Adam Gidwitz is the author of Max in the House of Spies, the Newbery Honor book The Inquisitor’s Tale, the New York Times bestseller A Tale Dark & Grimm and its companions, the bestselling Unicorn Rescue Society series, and the Star Wars novel The Empire Strikes Back: So You Want to Be a Jedi. He is also the creator and narrator of Grimm, Grimmer, Grimmest, a #1 podcast for young people, and he produced the Netflix animated adaptation of A Tale Dark & Grimm, which was nominated for an Emmy for Outstanding Animated Series. He lives in Brooklyn, NY, USA with his wife and daughter.

b: After a degree in Theatre from Smith College, Massachusetts, Adithi was assistant director on the Hindi film, Satya. An author, scriptwriter and playwright across genres and ages, the rights to her film script rests…
f: After a degree in Theatre from Smith College, Massachusetts, Adithi was assistant director on the Hindi film, Satya. An author, scriptwriter and playwright across genres and ages, the rights to her film script rests with Aamir Khan Productions. Her award-winning books include The Scent of Roses, Will Goondi Come Home?, Noon Chai and a Story, Candid Tales: India on a Motorcycle and Boy, Bear. Her newest—The Bhootbusters of Himmatnagar—(illustrated by Nandita Basu), is her first to be told in graphic novel format. Adithi conducts writing workshops, and is visiting faculty at the Srishti Manipal Institute of Art, Design and Technology. Delegate | 2018, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026 Speaker | 2025 | NLF Reading Challenge Making the Universal Personal A Dose of Optimism

b: Aditi De is a Bangalore-based author, dreamer, traveller and editor. She loves children and the world of the word. In 1989, she launched Junior Quest, the popular magazine from the Chandamama group, and later edited the…
f: Aditi De is a Bangalore-based author, dreamer, traveller and editor. She loves children and the world of the word. In 1989, she launched Junior Quest, the popular magazine from the Chandamama group, and later edited the Open Sesame children’s supplement at the Deccan Herald. Her books include A Twist in the Tale: More Indian Folktales, Jawaharlal nehru: The Jewel of India. She has written children’s columns for Chatterbox magazine, Deccan Chronicle and Young World. Cultural journalism has been her forte since her stints at Indian Express, Chennai, and Deccan Herald, Bangalore. Her passions in life include travel, interacting with creative people engaged in the arts, crafts and textiles, and sharing special time with children. Delegate | 2017, 2018, 2019

b: Shaikh has been writing since the age of eight and has published his poetry in a number of anthologies and journals. His autobiographical novel ‘The Library Girl’ was published in 2017. His recent children’s book…
f: Shaikh has been writing since the age of eight and has published his poetry in a number of anthologies and journals. His autobiographical novel ‘The Library Girl’ was published in 2017. His recent children’s book ‘Letters to Ammi’ came out in 2019. He has been awarded the Outstanding Achievement in Poetry Silver Award in 2003, the Ne8x Author of the Year Award 2019 and the Poiesis International Award for Excellence in Literature in 2020. He works as a teacher and translator residing presently in Thane. Delegate | 2020 | NLF Speaker | 2021 | NLF Reading Challenge Author Interaction | NLF Reading Challenge 2021 Book Reading: Letters to Ammi | 2020 Stories That Matter to Emerging Readers | 2020

b: Aijaz Khan’s debut film, The White Elephant (2009) premiered at the prestigious International Film Festival of India. Travelling to more than 10 film festivals including New York Film Festival and the UK Film Festival.…
f: Aijaz Khan’s debut film, The White Elephant (2009) premiered at the prestigious International Film Festival of India. Travelling to more than 10 film festivals including New York Film Festival and the UK Film Festival. Aijaz has been active in the advertising industry, directing and producing Ad films, for over a decade. Most recently, Aijaz directed Baankey Ki Crazy Baraat, which was well received at the Box Office. Delegate | 2019, 2020 Peripheries: Boundaries on the Edge, Boundaries Within | 2020

b: Akhila Das Blah is an author, entrepreneur and educationist specialising in diversity and inclusion with a focus on early childhood. She has authored 5 books for children and is a co-founder of Indigrow…
f: Akhila Das Blah is an author, entrepreneur and educationist specialising in diversity and inclusion with a focus on early childhood. She has authored 5 books for children and is a co-founder of Indigrow (www.indigrowkids.com), an organisation that helps parents and educators raise kids in an increasingly diverse world. She believes that when kids, parents and educators learn to celebrate differences and similarities in their early childhood years, we can challenge bias, educate and raise empowered as well as empathetic kids. Delegate | 2023

b: Akshay Gandhi is a theatre artist & practitioner, collaborating with artists in various disciplines to create performances. An alumni of Saratoga International Theatre Institute, New York and BITS-Pilani, he has also…
f: Akshay Gandhi is a theatre artist & practitioner, collaborating with artists in various disciplines to create performances. An alumni of Saratoga International Theatre Institute, New York and BITS-Pilani, he has also received extensive training with Indian Ensemble & Veena Basavarajaiah in theatre and movement arts. He is a recipient of prestigious Tata Scholar Grant and BITSAA 30u30 award for his work in performing arts. His recent work includes, Mahesh Dattani’s “Clearing the Rubble” & “Kaavad Katha” in India; Charles Mee’s “Adam & Evie” & “No Place” in New York, USA.His primary performance research is an investigation into classical performance practices with his collaborators: Sajan Sankaran (Dhrupad music) & Anand Satheendran (Kathakali Dancer) through the post-modern practice of Viewpoints along with his work in Kaavadkatha tradition. Delegate | 2018 Kaavad Katha Performance | 2018

b: Alastair Chisholm is a children’s author of sci-fi adventures Orion Lost , shortlisted for the Waterstones Children’s Book Prize, Adam-2 , the Blackwell’s Children’s Book of the Year, and I Am Wolf , nominated for the…
f: Alastair Chisholm is a children’s author of sci-fi adventures Orion Lost , shortlisted for the Waterstones Children’s Book Prize, Adam-2 , the Blackwell’s Children’s Book of the Year, and I Am Wolf , nominated for the Carnegie medal, as well as the Dragon Storm series of chapter books, and picture books including The Prince and the Witch and the Thief and the Bears and Inch and Grub , winner of the Queen’s Knickers Award. He lives in Edinburgh with his wife and family and a cat named Maudie, who is yowling at him even though there is CLEARLY food in her bowl, and his hobbies include writing, and playing games on his phone when he should be writing. He likes biscuits. Speaker | 2025 | NLF Reading Challenge

b: Ameen Haque is a storyteller, a story coach and the founder of Storywallahs. He can climb a mountain, walk miles and stay up all night to listen to a good story. He loves telling stories to children and playing table…
f: Ameen Haque is a storyteller, a story coach and the founder of Storywallahs. He can climb a mountain, walk miles and stay up all night to listen to a good story. He loves telling stories to children and playing table tennis. An occasional poet, he writes in both Hindi and English. When not telling a story, he can be found reading one. Delegate | 2019

f: Anand is the creative director of BYJU’s. He ran live game operations for some of the world’s largest and most famous social games, including Mafia Wars, Hidden Chronicles, Hidden Shadows and Yoville. He is one of India’s most widely published videogames columnists in the mainstream press, best known cricket satire columnists and has published a wide variety of satire columns in leading Indian publications. He is a published author with a range of children’s comics and stories for leading Indian publishers. His major areas of interests is the use of media like comics and videogames for education and awareness programs in the development sector. Delegate | 2017 How Games Make Kids Smarter | 2017

A ndaleeb’s recent novels All Drama No Queen and Mirror, Mirror were published by Penguin Random House and Duckbill respectively in 2021. She has an upcoming YA novel with Harper Collins. Delegate | 2017, 2018, 2022, 2023 A Dose of Optimism

b: Andrea Wang is an acclaimed author of children’s books. Her book Watercress was awarded the Caldecott Medal, a Newbery Honor, the Asian/Pacific American Award for Literature, a New England Book Award, and a Boston…
f: Andrea Wang is an acclaimed author of children’s books. Her book Watercress was awarded the Caldecott Medal, a Newbery Honor, the Asian/Pacific American Award for Literature, a New England Book Award, and a Boston Globe-Horn Book Honor. Her other books, The Many Meanings of Meilan, Magic Ramen , and The Nian Monster, have also received awards and starred reviews. Her work explores culture, creative thinking, and identity. She is also the author of seven nonfiction titles for the library and school market. Andrea holds an M.S. in Environmental Science and an M.F.A. in Creative Writing for Young People. She lives in Colorado with her family. Speaker | 2025 | NLF Reading Challenge

b: A former head of Middle School English, Angie Erickson currently works as the Head of Libraries at United World College of Southeast Asia in Singapore. She is interested in how educational leadership, curriculum design…
f: A former head of Middle School English, Angie Erickson currently works as the Head of Libraries at United World College of Southeast Asia in Singapore. She is interested in how educational leadership, curriculum design and workshop pedagogy can be integrated to create a school culture of reading, thinking and writing. For the past few years, she has been working to create systems to articulate classroom and departmental libraries to support the needs of all readers. She currently teaches one section of “The Imperfect Art of Living” a philosophy and design thinking course for the Innovation Academy Online. When she is not reading, Angie enjoys coffee, thru-hiking and playing the cello badly (to the consternation of her neighbors).

b: ANGIE as she prefers to be called, lives and speaks designs and loves experimenting with new ideas in baking, gardening, crochet, macrame and pottery. She is living proof that good things come in small packages as well…
f: ANGIE as she prefers to be called, lives and speaks designs and loves experimenting with new ideas in baking, gardening, crochet, macrame and pottery. She is living proof that good things come in small packages as well as a paradox who is always dreaming big. When she passes the age of 50, she plans on making it big as a ceramic artist. In her quest to see something new, Angie loves travelling and meeting new people. The more she does this, the more it affirms her belief that humans are not of this planet. Presently, Angie serves as a co-founder of ‘The Other Design Studio,’ a creative venture she embarked upon with her husband Upesh, an endeavors that has flourished for more than two decades. Angie have taken on the role of managing trustees at an autism school in Bangalore, where she active engagement extends to fundraising and networking responsibilities. Delegate | 2023

b: Anita Nair is an Indian best-selling author of fiction and poetry, with her famous novels The Better Man and Ladies Coupe translated into 21 languages. Her first book, a collection of short stories called Satyr of the…
f: Anita Nair is an Indian best-selling author of fiction and poetry, with her famous novels The Better Man and Ladies Coupe translated into 21 languages. Her first book, a collection of short stories called Satyr of the Subway won her a fellowship from the Virginia Center for the Creative Arts. In 2002, appeared the collection of poems Malabar Mind, and in 2003 Where the Rain is Born – Writings about Kerala which she has edited. Anita has also written The Puffin Book of Myths and Legends (2004). She also edited Where the Rain is Born (2003). Anita’s writings about Kerala and her poetry has been included in The Poetry India Collection and a British Council Poetry Workshop Anthology. Her other works include Mistress (2003), Adventures of Nonu, the Skating Squirrel (2006), Living Next Door to Alise (2007), Magical Indian Myths (2008), Cut Like Wound (2012), The Lilac House (2012), Idris: Keeper of The Light (2014), Chain of Custody (2015), and Alphabet Soup for Lovers (2016). Delegate | 2017, 2023, 2025 Speaker | 2024 | NLF Reading Challenge Author Interaction | NLF Reading Challenge 2024

b: Anita Roy is a writer, editor and environmentalist based in Somerset, UK. She is the author of several books including ‘Gravepyres School for the Recently Deceased’, and co-edited ‘Gifts of Gravity and Light: A Nature…
f: Anita Roy is a writer, editor and environmentalist based in Somerset, UK. She is the author of several books including ‘Gravepyres School for the Recently Deceased’, and co-edited ‘Gifts of Gravity and Light: A Nature Almanac for the 21st Century.’ She plays an active role in her local environmental group, Transition Town Wellington. She lived in Delhi for 20 years, and founded and ran the young adult and children’s imprint, Young Zubaan. Delegate | 2021 Author Interaction | NLF Reading Challenge 2021

b: Anita Vachharajani has a Masters in English Literature and in Linguistics. She has just published a pictorial biography for Young Adults called ‘Amrita Sher-Gil: Rebel with a Paintbrush’. She has written newspaper…
f: Anita Vachharajani has a Masters in English Literature and in Linguistics. She has just published a pictorial biography for Young Adults called ‘Amrita Sher-Gil: Rebel with a Paintbrush’. She has written newspaper columns and book reviews. Her stories for children have appeared in ‘The Puffin Book of Bedtime Stories’, ‘The Puffin Book of Spooky Ghost Stories’, and in various picture books, like ‘Nonie’s Magic Quilt’, ‘Ambili’, ‘Nayana and the Not-so-scary Owl’ and ‘Tara Tambe, Forest Friend’. Her translations of traditional rhymes feature in ‘The Tenth Rasa: the Penguin Book of Indian Nonsense Verse’. She has collaborated with her husband Amit Vachharajani on ‘Amazing India’, a pictorial description of the 29 states of India. Delegate | 2018, 2019

b: Anitha Murthy is a software consultant by profession and loves to write. She dabbles in various genres, from short stories to poetry to novellas, both in print and online. Her books for children have been published by…
f: Anitha Murthy is a software consultant by profession and loves to write. She dabbles in various genres, from short stories to poetry to novellas, both in print and online. Her books for children have been published by Pratham and Talking Cub. Delegate | 2021

b: Ankit Chadha, a writer and storyteller, specialized in weaving new narratives for Dastangoi – the art of storytelling. His writing varied from biographical accounts of personalities like Kabir and Majaaz; to modern folk…
f: Ankit Chadha, a writer and storyteller, specialized in weaving new narratives for Dastangoi – the art of storytelling. His writing varied from biographical accounts of personalities like Kabir and Majaaz; to modern folk tales on nomadic pastoralism and the Internet. He had spoken on Dastans at platforms including Princeton, Harvard and Yale. Additionally, Ankit had innovated the form of musical narrative that uniquely brings together stories and music. He had also worked on Urdu adaptations of children’s classics including Alice, The Little Prince and Phantom Tollbooth. Ankit is the author of the award-winning books “Amir Khusrau – The Man in Riddles” and “My Gandhi Story”. Delegate | 2017 Trend vs Tradition | 2017

b: Ann was Librarian at CLPE (Centre for Literacy in Primary Education) in London for 29 years. She previously worked in school & public libraries. Ann was centrally involved in reviving the UK section of IBBY…
f: Ann was Librarian at CLPE (Centre for Literacy in Primary Education) in London for 29 years. She previously worked in school & public libraries. Ann was centrally involved in reviving the UK section of IBBY (International Board on Books for Young People) in the mid 1990s and served as secretary then chair of the section and was on the international executive 2004-2008. She was co-director of the IBBY Congress in London in 2012 and is still on the IBBY UK committee. She completed an MA in Children’s Literature at Roehampton University in 2005. Since retiring from CLPE in March 2021 she has continued to be involved in a variety of voluntary projects both within and outside the children’s book world.

b: Anthony John McGowan is an English author of books for children, teenagers and adults. He is the winner of the 2020 CILIP Carnegie Medal for Lark . In addition to his 2020 win, he has been twice longlisted (for The…
f: Anthony John McGowan is an English author of books for children, teenagers and adults. He is the winner of the 2020 CILIP Carnegie Medal for Lark . In addition to his 2020 win, he has been twice longlisted (for The Knife That Killed Me in 2008 and Brock in 2014) and once shortlisted (for Rook in 2018) for the CILIP Carnegie Medal, and is the winner of the 2006 Booktrust Teenage Prize for Henry Tumour. Delegate | 2025 Speaker | 2021 | NLF Reading Challenge Author Interaction | NLF Reading Challenge 2021

b: Anupam Arunachalam is a Delhi-based writer, illustrator and comic book artist. His work has been published by Penguin Random House India, Hachette India, Tinkle, Comixense, Pratham Books, Mint and Campfire Graphic…
f: Anupam Arunachalam is a Delhi-based writer, illustrator and comic book artist. His work has been published by Penguin Random House India, Hachette India, Tinkle, Comixense, Pratham Books, Mint and Campfire Graphic Novels among others. f: Anuradha Ruhil Barua has extensive experience teaching the IB Diploma. She is passionate about language (s) and teaches English and Hindi. Her goal is to help students grow as readers and individuals by creating a collaborative classroom culture. Her educational background includes an MA in German Studies and a PhD in Second Language Acquisition and Teaching.The languages of her home are Hindi, Assamese and English. She lives and works in Singapore. Delegate | 2018, 2019, 2020, 2021, 2022 The Power of Language – Shrinking expression | 2019

b: Anuradha Sengupta is a writer and editor whose work has appeared in CNN, Gulf News, NYC-based Women’s Media Center, The Hindu, among other platforms. She is founder-editor of Jalebi Ink, an award-winning media…
f: Anuradha Sengupta is a writer and editor whose work has appeared in CNN, Gulf News, NYC-based Women’s Media Center, The Hindu, among other platforms. She is founder-editor of Jalebi Ink, an award-winning media collective for children and youth. Her portfolio includes reportage from Kuwait after the Gulf War and a citizens’ media project in Afghanistan. She is currently working on a book on food folklore from India. Delegate | 2018

b: Aparna Karthikeyan is an author, independent journalist and senior fellow, People’s Archive of Rural India (PARI). She has written five books for children: Cat’s Egg (Karadi Tales), Kali Wants to Dance (Pratham Books),…
f: Aparna Karthikeyan is an author, independent journalist and senior fellow, People’s Archive of Rural India (PARI). She has written five books for children: Cat’s Egg (Karadi Tales), Kali Wants to Dance (Pratham Books), Woof! Adventures by the Sea (Red Panda), No Nonsense Nandhini (Karadi Tales-PARI collaboration) and Looking for Laddoo (Karadi Tales). She has produced text articles, photo essays and video documentaries for various platforms, including The Hindu, PARI, The Caravan, The Wire and Scroll. Her non-fiction book, Nine Rupees an Hour (Context) documents ten disappearing livelihoods of Tamil Nadu. Aparna lives with her family and two dogs in Chennai, the city she calls home. Delegate | 2021 Distilling Myths, History, and Little-Known Realities | 2021

b: Archana Garodia Gupta with a lifelong passion for books, languages, travel and history, Archana has a knack for weaving delightful nuggets of information into engaging tales. A leading national quizzer, she has won the…
f: Archana Garodia Gupta with a lifelong passion for books, languages, travel and history, Archana has a knack for weaving delightful nuggets of information into engaging tales. A leading national quizzer, she has won the ‘Champion of Champions’ title from BBC Mastermind India. She regularly writes articles on history and business for magazines, and was seen on national television as a member of the expert panel on Kaun Banega Crorepati. She was the national president of the FICCI Ladies Organization (FLO) in 2015–16, where she set up many programmes for the empowerment of Indian women. Archana was raised in New Delhi and holds an MBA from IIM, Ahmedabad. She lives in Delhi where she and her husband run a jewellery business under the Touchstone brand. Her new book, The Women Who Ruled India, has just been released. Delegate | 2019 History Quest – A fun quiz on Indian history | 2019 Stories Told/Suppressed Part 2 | 2019

b: Arefa Tehsin is the author of several fiction and non-fiction books and contributes to various publications like The Indian Express, The Hindu, Deccan Herald, Scroll.in and Outlook Money. Her picture book The Elephant…
f: Arefa Tehsin is the author of several fiction and non-fiction books and contributes to various publications like The Indian Express, The Hindu, Deccan Herald, Scroll.in and Outlook Money. Her picture book The Elephant Bird was read at 3200+ locations in India from the slums to the Presidential library on the International Literacy Day, 2016 and translated in more than 40 languages. Her books have been shortlisted for awards like FICCI Best Book of the Year Award, Neev Book Award and The Hindu-Goodbooks Best Author Award. Arefa spent her childhood treading jungles with her naturalist father Raza Tehsin, exploring caves and chasing snakes. She was appointed the Honorary Wildlife Warden of Udaipur and has pursued nature conservation through her writings. Delegate | 2019, 2021, 2022 Building Empathy and Self Awareness | 2019 Growing Boundaries: Relationships, Neighbourhoods & Questions | 2021 A Childhood as a Naturalist’s Daughter

b: Arti Sonthalia is a Hyderabad based children’s author. She started her journey with “Chicken Soup For the Soul” books, and continued to the children’s genre. Her debut children’s book, Big Bully And M-me was nominated…
f: Arti Sonthalia is a Hyderabad based children’s author. She started her journey with “Chicken Soup For the Soul” books, and continued to the children’s genre. Her debut children’s book, Big Bully And M-me was nominated for the Crystal Kite Asia award. Her other books, Hungry to Read has inspired even the reluctant readers to read. Her book Best Friends Forever has won the FICCI Book of The Year Award Jan’20 and her latest book Hungry To Play is loved by all. She has also been a TEDx speaker. She is an avid reader, music lover, bathroom singer and a writer at heart. When Sonthalia is not writing she is busy listening to music and reading. Sonthalia loves long walks and enjoys chocolates too! Delegate | 2020 Book Reading: Hungry to Play | 2020 Stories That Matter to Emerging Readers | 2020

b: Aruna Sankaranarayanan currently writes for The Hindu, Deccan Herald, and Financial Express (Digital) on teaching, learning, work, relationships, and well-being. She authors a monthly column, Youth, that addresses…
f: Aruna Sankaranarayanan currently writes for The Hindu, Deccan Herald, and Financial Express (Digital) on teaching, learning, work, relationships, and well-being. She authors a monthly column, Youth, that addresses issues of young adults and blogs at www.arunasankaranarayanan.com. Her first book, Zero Limits: Things Every 20 Something Should Know, will be published by Rupa Publications in 2020. She was the Founder & Director of PRAYATNA, a centre for children with learning difficulties for 22 years. Aruna holds a doctorate in Psychology. Delegate | 2020 NLF Imaginary Lines Book Club for Parents and Educators: Reader Come Home by Maryanne Wolf | Session 1 | 2020

b: Asha Nehemiah writes for children ages 3 years to 12 years. Her published work spans picture books, early literacy books, books for emerging readers. chapter books, middle-grade fiction and short stories. Asha’s books…
f: Asha Nehemiah writes for children ages 3 years to 12 years. Her published work spans picture books, early literacy books, books for emerging readers. chapter books, middle-grade fiction and short stories. Asha’s books are loved for their humour, exciting plots and spirit of adventure. Her fiction also touches upon issues such as inclusion, diversity and gender parity. She believes that stories are the best way for everyone, especially children, to explore new ideas and cultures. She writes in English and her books have been translated into several Indian and global languages. Delegate | 2017, 2022, 2024 The Grandest Bond

b: Ashim Ahluwalia is a director, writer, and producer. His debut, “John & Jane”, premiered at the Toronto and Berlin Film Festivals and was HBO Films’ first Indian release. “Miss Lovely” was an official selection at the…
f: Ashim Ahluwalia is a director, writer, and producer. His debut, “John & Jane”, premiered at the Toronto and Berlin Film Festivals and was HBO Films’ first Indian release. “Miss Lovely” was an official selection at the Cannes Film Festival, followed by “Daddy,” a biopic on gangster Arun Gawli, featuring Arjun Rampal and Farhan Akhtar. His latest Netflix series “CLA$$” explores wealth disparity and social dynamics in an elite New Delhi school. Ahluwalia was named “one of the ten best emerging film directors working today” by Phaidon Press in “Take 100: The Future of Film”, and is the only Indian filmmaker to have had films premiere in the official selections of Cannes, Berlin, Venice, Toronto, and SXSW festivals. Delegate | 2023

b: Ashwitha Jayakumar has written and adapted over a dozen books for young readers on history, mythology and science. Since graduating with an MSc in Literature and Society: 1688–1900 from the University of Edinburgh and…
f: Ashwitha Jayakumar has written and adapted over a dozen books for young readers on history, mythology and science. Since graduating with an MSc in Literature and Society: 1688–1900 from the University of Edinburgh and an MA in Medieval Studies from the University of Leeds, she’s worn many different hats, from editor to high school English teacher, research consultant, and writer. She loves all things historical and fantastical and lives in New Delhi, in a house overflowing with books.

f: Bhajju Shyam was born in Pattangarh, in Madhya Pradesh in Central India in 1971. Sixteen-year-old Bhajju left his village and came to Bhopal in search of work. As Bhajju’s talent became apparent, Jangarh encouraged Bhajju to strike out on his own. Bhajju’s work soon became known throughout India, and his first international exposure came in 1998 when he was part of a group exhibition at the Musee des Arts Decoratifs in Paris. Since then his work has been shown in the UK, Germany, Holland and Russia. In 2001, he received a state award for Best Indigenous Artist. He has ten books to his credit and his best-known work, The London Jungle Book, is a visual travelogue of his 2002 visit to London, where he went to paint the interior of an up-market Indian restaurant. The book, published by Tara Books and the Museum of London, was released in November 2004, along with a three-month exhibition at the Museum. Bhajju has received many awards: In 2001, he received a state award for Best Indigenous Artist (Madhya Pradesh), CRESCER Magazine 30 Best Children’s Book Award Brazil in 2011 and the Ojas Art Award in 2015. Cumulatively, his books have sold nearly a 100,000 copies, worldwide and have been made available in multiple languages.

b: Nandini Bajpai grew up in New Delhi, India, one of four sisters and many cousins, in a family that liked to read. She lived and worked in India, Australia, and the US, before settling in the Boston area with her…
f: Nandini Bajpai grew up in New Delhi, India, one of four sisters and many cousins, in a family that liked to read. Delegate | 2020 Book Reading: A Match Made in Mehendi | 2020 The Reading of Young Adult Books in India | 2020

b: Nandini Nayar is the award-winning author of over 60 books for children of all ages. She is one of the most prolific children’s writers of India, with books published by well-known Indian publishers. What Shall I Make?…
f: Nandini Nayar is the award-winning author of over 60 books for children of all ages. She is one of the most prolific children’s writers of India, with books published by well-known Indian publishers. What Shall I Make? was named an outstanding book by the United States Board on Books for Young Readers. Pranav’s Picture, What Shall I Make?, Guddu’s Photo and The House of Fourteen Cats feature in the list of books recommended by the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE). What Shall I Make? and What Did You See? feature in 101 Indian Children’s Books We Love (Zubaan). Her early chapter book, Mini’s Questions, was on the recently announced Parag Honour List 2021. Delegate | 2021 Growing Boundaries: Relationships, Neighbourhoods & Questions | 2021

b: Nandini Sen Gupta is an award-winning writer of historical fiction and narrative history. Her book credits include The Blue Horse And Other Amazing Animals from Indian History (publisher Hachette), winner of the Sahitya…
f: Nandini Sen Gupta is an award-winning writer of historical fiction and narrative history. Her book credits include The Blue Horse And Other Amazing Animals from Indian History (publisher Hachette), winner of the Sahitya Akademi Bal Puraskar 2024. Earlier the book had been shortlisted for Auther Awards 2021 in children’s fiction category and selected for the prestigious Parag Honour List. Her other works include The King Within, The Poisoned Heart & The Ocean’s Own, Book I, II & III of the Gupta Empire Trilogy published by HarperCollins India and The Story of Kalidas: The Gem Among Poets published by Eicher Goodearth Publications. Her first narrative non-fiction biography, Rani Durgawati: The Forgotten Life of a Warrior Queen published by Penguin India, debuted to widespread acclaim in November 2022.

b: I am an independent science communicator, journalist, and author. After working at The Hindu and Brainwave magazine, I co-founded the feminist science multimedia platform The​Life​of​Science​.com which covers the…
f: I am an independent science communicator, journalist, and author. After working at The Hindu and Brainwave magazine, I co-founded the feminist science multimedia platform The​Life​of​Science​.com which covers the research and journeys of underrepresented groups in Indian science, and reports on issues of access and inequity that exist within the STEM community. I have also helped set up a children’s library in Mangalore, where I coordinated several virtual reading-based activities for children during the lockdowns. My work has been published on platforms such as The Wire, Firstpost, ThePrint, Mongabay-India and Caravan. I have along the way authored a few children’s books, the latest being The World that Mai Built (Pratham Books), Rathna and the Ring of Fire (Pratham Books), 31 Fantastic Adventures in Science (co-authored by Aashima Dogra; Puffin Books), and Anna’s Extraordinary Experiments with Weather (Pratham Books). I love bird watching, trying out different kinds of food and I have a burgeoning interest in natural building. Delegate | 2022

b: Writing has been my passion since a very young age. As a child, jotting down little adventures and turning rhyming words into verses of poems was something that came naturally to me and really excited me! Currently…
f: Writing has been my passion since a very young age. As a child, jotting down little adventures and turning rhyming words into verses of poems was something that came naturally to me and really excited me! Currently studying creative writing at Srishti, I aspire to gradually develop my skills and be better with this thing that I love to do, with every passing year. Delegate | 2019

b: Naseeruddin Shah is an Indian film and stage actor whose performances have won him critical acclaim and garnered several prestigious awards including the Padma Shri (1987) and the Padma Bhushan (2003). Motley was formed…
f: Naseeruddin Shah is an Indian film and stage actor whose performances have won him critical acclaim and garnered several prestigious awards including the Padma Shri (1987) and the Padma Bhushan (2003). Motley was formed by Naseeruddin Shah and Benjamin Gilani in 1979. Their well known plays include Herman Wouk’s, The Caine Mutiny, Samuel Beckett’s Waiting for Godot, and the adaptation of Julius Caesar.

b: An award-winning children’s books author, Natasha Sharma began her writing journey with the ever-popular book ‘Icky, Yucky, Mucky’. With eighteen books to her credit, Natasha has written across age groups and formats…
f: An award-winning children’s books author, Natasha Sharma began her writing journey with the ever-popular book ‘Icky, Yucky, Mucky’. With eighteen books to her credit, Natasha has written across age groups and formats from picture books, early chapter books, historical fiction to her new book in a graphic novel format, ‘The Good Indian Child’s Guide to Eating Mangoes’. Her awards received include Best Illustrated Children’s Book in Comic Con India 2018 for Shah Jahan and the Ruby Robber. The South Asia Book Award in 2015 for ‘Razia and the Pesky Presents’. The SCBWI Crystal Kite Award for Asia and Middle East in 2014 for Bonkers. Natasha wields humour on the page and her stories are known to lead to many giggles. Delegate | 2019 The Power of Language – Shrinking expression | 2019 Pros and Cons of a Set Formula | 2019

b: Nayanika spent her childhood following her parents across many incredible parts of India. Though she harboured dreams of becoming a stage actor, she followed the proverbial left side of her brain to do an MBA at IIM…
f: Nayanika spent her childhood following her parents across many incredible parts of India. Though she harboured dreams of becoming a stage actor, she followed the proverbial left side of her brain to do an MBA at IIM Bengaluru and became an investment banker. A decade later, she followed her heart to live in Africa. Since then, she’s been following the right side of her brain and is a copywriter by day and a storyteller by night. She now lives in London with her husband, two daughters and their goldfish named Sushi and Fishfinger – who spend their days following each other. Mostly. Nayanika has been invited as a speaker at the Jaipur Literature Festival in 2015, 2016 and 2017 in Jaipur and at London. She has conducted readings and children’s workshops at the Southbank Centre in London, at libraries and bookstores – and pretty much anywhere that she can find children who might lend her an ear! She has spoken extensively at schools in author interactions, and hopes to see children engage more with not only the written word, but with the wondrous world of nature. Delegate | 2018

b: Nazia Erum is the critically acclaimed author of the book Mothering A Muslim. Her work around inter-faith harmony has found mention in the Gaurdian, Washington Post amongst many other national and international news…
f: Nazia Erum is the critically acclaimed author of the book Mothering A Muslim. Her work around inter-faith harmony has found mention in the Gaurdian, Washington Post amongst many other national and international news services. Presently she is heading Media and Advocacy for Amnesty International in India. Delegate | 2019 Conflicts that Matter | 2019

b: Nazima Pathan was born in India and raised in London, moving later to Cambridge where she lives with her husband and two children. She is a children’s doctor and researcher, but has always enjoyed reading and writing…
f: Nazima Pathan was born in India and raised in London, moving later to Cambridge where she lives with her husband and two children. She is a children’s doctor and researcher, but has always enjoyed reading and writing stories. (After all, science—when conveyed well—is a tale of the why’s, the how’s and therefore’s.) But children’s stories are special, important and fun, and after learning the craft of writing fiction, Nazima found a home in creating magical stories for curious children who believe in the right to dream. Dream Hunters is her debut novel; its much-anticipated sequel, The Night Curse , will be released in July 2025. Speaker | 2025 | NLF Reading Challenge

b: Neha Singh is a Mumbai based children’s author and has written five books for children so far. ‘The Wednesday Bazaar’ and ‘Bela Misses Her Train’ with Karadi Tales, ‘Moongphali’ for Rupa and Co., ‘Its Playtime’ for…
f: Neha Singh is a Mumbai based children’s author and has written five books for children so far. ‘The Wednesday Bazaar’ and ‘Bela Misses Her Train’ with Karadi Tales, ‘Moongphali’ for Rupa and Co., ‘Its Playtime’ for Pratham’s Storyweaver and her latest offering ‘I Need to Pee’ with Puffin, India. She contributes poems and stories in Hindi to Bhopal based children’s magazines Chakmak and Pluto. She conducts sessions around her books with children across India, in literature festivals, theatre festivals and also as part of outreach programs. Apart from writing, Neha is a theatre practitioner. She has worked in over fifteen professional theatre productions in Mumbai as an actor, playwright, producer and director. She runs her own theatre production company called ‘Rahi Theatre Company’ and has produced two plays under her banner; ‘DohriZindagi’ and ‘Jhalkari’.Neha is a women’s rights activist and spearheads a movement called ‘Why loiter?’, which aims at reclaiming public spaces for women, and is currently in its fourth year since conception. Her other interests include filmmaking, Indian classical music and Kalaripayattu. Delegate | 2018

b: After years working around the world as a Creative Director, Neil now lives in Goa where he makes art; takes film photographs; writes comics, novels and screenplays; makes music; does pottery; listens to his vinyl…
f: After years working around the world as a Creative Director, Neil now lives in Goa where he makes art; takes film photographs; writes comics, novels and screenplays; makes music; does pottery; listens to his vinyl collection; cooks up elaborate meals; and writes and develops kids’ stories. Do not ask him about a TV series, even a limited one, because he has no idea of that world. A record from 1969 on the other hand. Neil uses humour in his stories. So do not read them to kids at bedtime or they won’t sleep. His books are full of imagination. You’ll meet characters like a Donut offering Free Hugs. Or a Hipsquirrot – that’s a mix of a Hippo, Squirrel and Parrot. His first book was nominated for Book of the year at the CBC Awards in Australia. He’s released three books with Hachette India in the last year.

f: Nidhi is an advocate of responsible media & technology. She has spent over 20 years in content, editorial, brand and data analytics across organisations in India, UAE, Greece and UK. f: Nikhil Gulati is a writer and illustrator of comic books and graphic novels. He believes in telling stories that evoke wonder, promote compassion and give meaning to life. He has published graphic books with Puffin, Pratham Books and his most recent graphic novel, the People of the Indus, with Penguin Random House, India. Delegate | 2023

b: Nitin Kushalappa is the author of A Hoysala Adventure, a children’s historical fiction published as part of the ‘Girls of India’ series in 2025 by Puffin Books. He also authored Dakshin: South Indian Myths and Fables…
f: Nitin Kushalappa is the author of A Hoysala Adventure, a children’s historical fiction published as part of the ‘Girls of India’ series in 2025 by Puffin Books. He also authored Dakshin: South Indian Myths and Fables Retold, a children’s book collection of 15 South Indian folktales, published in 2023, again by Puffin Books. Dakshin won the 2025 Bal Sahitya Puraskar (awarded by the Sahitya Akademi), and was shortlisted for the 2023 Atta Galatta-Bangalore Literature Festival Award. His various articles have been published by the Deccan Herald and Star of Mysore, under the names Mookonda Kushalappa and Mookonda Nitin Kushalappa. Kushalappa wrote books on local history, a translation from Kannada on a Gandhian freedom fighter, a biography of a decorated army hero, and a novella. He has worked for the online Sandooka Kodava Virtual Museum and on an old temple script, called thirke.

b: Niveditha Subramaniam is a writer-illustrator based in Chennai. She cherishes every opportunity to celebrate her abiding love for visuals and particularly loves silent or nearly wordless narratives. She has published 14…
f: Niveditha Subramaniam is a writer-illustrator based in Chennai. She cherishes every opportunity to celebrate her abiding love for visuals and particularly loves silent or nearly wordless narratives. She has published 14 books, ranging from picture books to teen-fiction and a graphic novel for young adults. Niveditha is a Charles Wallace India Trust Scholar (2015 – 2017) and a recipient of the Bal Sahitya Puraskar (2015). Six of her titles have been recommended by the CBSE and 2 by the NCERT for schools. Delegate | 2018, 2020

b: Niyatee Sharma combines her love of writing for children and her expertise in design to create much loved stories and picture books. Her books include ‘The Runaway Peacock’ (Parag Honour List 2020) and ‘Harvest Day’ and…
f: Niyatee Sharma combines her love of writing for children and her expertise in design to create much loved stories and picture books. Her books include ‘The Runaway Peacock’ (Parag Honour List 2020) and ‘Harvest Day’ and ‘What Can I Be?’ (Toka Box top south Asian picture books 2020 & 2022) and ‘The Tomato Flood’. She is usually found tending to her vegetable garden or curled up with a book and her two adorable cats. Delegate | 2023

b: Olivier Lafont is a French author, screenplay writer, and actor living in Paris. His first fantasy novel Warrior was published by Penguin Random House. His other works include Oop and Lila Lost in the Scarabean, Sweet…
f: Olivier Lafont is a French author, screenplay writer, and actor living in Paris. His first fantasy novel Warrior was published by Penguin Random House. His other works include Oop and Lila Lost in the Scarabean, Sweet Revenge, Snowbound, and Purgatory: The Gun of God. He has written an Indo-French feature film that premiered at the Toronto Film Festival and went on to win seven awards internationally. He has acted in Hollywood and Indian films, including 3 Idiots and Guzaarish. He graduated with degrees in English Literature and in Theatre from Colgate University, USA, with academic distinction. Delegate | 2020 Book Reading: The Rise of the Midnight King | 2020 The Growing Complexity of Junior Readers in India | 2020

b: Pablo Cartaya is a New York Times bestselling author, screenwriter, actor, and speaker. His work has been featured in the New York Times, the Washington Post, NBC, and on Oprah’s Booklist. Pablo has worked with Disney,…
f: Pablo Cartaya is a New York Times bestselling author, screenwriter, actor, and speaker. His work has been featured in the New York Times, the Washington Post, NBC, and on Oprah’s Booklist. Pablo has worked with Disney, Apple TV+, and Sesame Street on projects adapted from television series and features. His novels, plays, and translations have been published by Penguin Random House, HarperCollins, McGraw Hill, and Disney Publishing Worldwide. Most recent novels include: A Hero’s Guide to Summer Vacation; The Epic Fail of Arturo Zamora, Marcus Vega Doesn’t Speak Spanish, Each Tiny Spark, the climate dystopia The Last Beekeeper, the graphic novel Curveball, and several forthcoming film and television projects. Visit him at: www.pablocartaya.com

b: Padma Venkatraman is an American writer and oceanographer who has lived in 5 countries, visited many more and explored rainforests on remote islands. She was chief scientist on research vessels, and decided to share the…
f: Padma Venkatraman is an American writer and oceanographer who has lived in 5 countries, visited many more and explored rainforests on remote islands. She was chief scientist on research vessels, and decided to share the sea of stories within her, through her books, as she sailed through life with her family. All her books have been featured on numerous best book lists, received a total of over 20 starred reviews, and won multiple honors (ALA Notable books, NYPL Notable, Kirkus Best Book, Booklist Editor’s Choice, SLJ Best Book, PW Flying Start, etc.) and awards (including two South Asia Book Awards, two Paterson prizes, a Julia Ward Howe Boston Authors Club Award, SCBWI Golden Kite award and many more).

b: Pallavi Jain is a Chartered Accountant and an alumnus of the National Institute of Design, Ahmedabad. Her journey to become a designer and illustrator has been led by a penchant for art & imagination and the purpose of…
f: Pallavi Jain is a Chartered Accountant and an alumnus of the National Institute of Design, Ahmedabad. Her journey to become a designer and illustrator has been led by a penchant for art & imagination and the purpose of bringing positive change. She works as a consultant to build brands as well as businesses and is an avid creator who loves to dabble in different artistic mediums. Pallavi also teaches at premier design institutes in India. She believes children inspire change for a better tomorrow. In her illustrations for children’s books, she loves to draw from various experiences and environments to create a magical world of her own. Delegate | 2022

b: Pankaj Saikia is an illustrator and children’s book author hailing from Assam. As an illustrator he is primarily focused on specializing in picture books and graphic novels for children. He has authored two picture…
f: Pankaj Saikia is an illustrator and children’s book author hailing from Assam. As an illustrator he is primarily focused on specializing in picture books and graphic novels for children. He has authored two picture books and has illustrated many others. His wordless picture Book “Theatre of Ghosts” has been listed in the PARAG HONOUR LIST 2023. More recently his work has been exhibited in Singapore under Asian Festival of Children’s book content 2023. Currently he lives and works from his studio in Guwahati, Assam.

b: Parvati Sharma is a Delhi-based author. Her debut was a collection of short stories called “The Dead Camel and Other Stories of Love”. She has also written a novel, “Close to Home”; a historical biography, “Jahangir: An…
f: Parvati Sharma is a Delhi-based author. Her debut was a collection of short stories called “The Dead Camel and Other Stories of Love”. She has also written a novel, “Close to Home”; a historical biography, “Jahangir: An Intimate Portrait of a Great Mughal”; and two books for children, “The Story of Babur” and “Rattu & Poorie’s Adventures in History: 1857”. Delegate | 2020 Book Reading: Rattu and Poorie’s Adventures in History: 1857 | 2020 Stories That Matter to Emerging Readers | 2020

b: Patrice was born in Brighton, England, raised in an Italian-Trinidadian family in mid-Sussex, and now lives on the South Coast. Her debut YA novel, Orangeboy, won the Bookseller YA Prize and the Waterstones Prize for…
f: Patrice was born in Brighton, England, raised in an Italian-Trinidadian family in mid-Sussex, and now lives on the South Coast. Her debut YA novel, Orangeboy, won the Bookseller YA Prize and the Waterstones Prize for Older Children’s Fiction and was shortlisted for the Costa Children’s Book Award. Her subsequent novels have been much acclaimed and frequent visitors to prize lists. Eight Pieces of Silva, published by Hodder in August 2020, won the Jhalak Children’s and Young Adult Prize 2021. Patrice has been nominated for the Carnegie Medal six times. Patrice was also awarded an MBE for services to literature in the Queen’s birthday honours 2021. Author Interaction | NLF Reading Challenge 2022

b: Payal Kapadia loves words for the stories they tell, even more for the stories they carry inside them. She studied English Literature at St Xavier’s College, Mumbai, and earned an M.Sc. degree (Journalism) from…
f: Payal Kapadia loves words for the stories they tell, even more for the stories they carry inside them. She studied English Literature at St Xavier’s College, Mumbai, and earned an M.Sc. degree (Journalism) from Northwestern University. Writing for news outlets in the United States, Hong Kong, Japan, and India, she was drawn to offbeat tales of unsung heroes and lost causes. Her debut novella Wisha Wozzariter won the 2013 Crossword Book Award for Children’s Writing and is in the 101 Indian Children’s Books We Love! compilation. Her best-selling books include the well-loved Horrid High series; a children’s biography of B.R. Ambedkar; Twice Upon a Time and Maidless in Mumbai . Payal now lives somewhere in Mumbai, in a flat among flats in a high-rise among high-rises in a street among streets. But she can see the sea from her window and sometimes it is big enough to swallow the sky and the clouds tumble into it. On those days, she writes. Delegate | 2019, 2024 Triggering Imagination | 2019

b: Peter has always loved telling stories. Growing up in New Jersey, he told stories by drawing whimsical characters and scenes from his imagination. As a teenager, he fell in love with writing and began telling his tales…
f: Peter has always loved telling stories. Growing up in New Jersey, he told stories by drawing whimsical characters and scenes from his imagination. As a teenager, he fell in love with writing and began telling his tales with words. While studying illustration at Art Center College of Design, Peter’s love of both words and pictures led him to take several courses on children’s books, and before long he knew he’d found his calling. After graduating from Art Center Peter moved to New York City to be closer to the publishing industry. He was working on animated TV shows when he signed a book deal to write and illustrate his first picture book, Flight of the Dodo. Peter quickly signed up his second and third books, and his career as an author and illustrator of children’s books was under way. Since then Peter has written and illustrated many books for children including The Wild Robot Trilogy, Children Make Terrible Pets and The Curious Garden. He is the recipient of a Caldecott Honor for Creepy Carrots! and has earned numerous honors, including a Horn Book Award, two E.B. White Awards, two E.B. White Honors, a Children’s Choice Award for Illustrator of the Year, two Irma Black Honors, a Golden Kite Award, a New York Times Best Illustrated Book Award and multiple New York Times bestsellers. Peter lives in Maine with his wife, Susan, son, Calvin, and their dog, Pam. Speaker | 2024 | NLF Reading Challenge Author Interaction | NLF Reading Challenge 2024

b: P.G. Bell is a native of South Wales, where he was raised on a diet of Greek mythology, ghost stories and Doctor Who. He’s had all sorts of jobs over the years, from lifeguard to roller coaster operator, but all he’s…
f: P.G. Bell is a native of South Wales, where he was raised on a diet of Greek mythology, ghost stories and Doctor Who. He’s had all sorts of jobs over the years, from lifeguard to roller coaster operator, but all he’s ever really wanted to do is write stories for a living. And now he does! He lives in Wales with his wife Anna, and their two children. Delegate | 2019 Triggering Imagination | 2019 The Power of Language – Shrinking Vocabularies | 2019

b: Pika Nani is the author of the newly released ‘The Adventures of Shrilok Homeless’, a detective thriller set in Mumbai. Her first book ‘Little Indians – Stories from across the country’, is a bestselling fact plus…
f: Pika Nani is the author of the newly released ‘The Adventures of Shrilok Homeless’, a detective thriller set in Mumbai. Her first book ‘Little Indians – Stories from across the country’, is a bestselling fact plus fiction book. Two of her stories appear in the popular text book Gul Mohar Reader. She worked as an organisational psychologist for several year before setting out to pursue her childhood dream of being a writer, hence the pen name from her childhood. She conducts creative writing workshops and book related activities in schools and libraries. She lives in Bengaluru with her family. Delegate | 2018, 2019, 2024 Can You Think Like Sherlock | 2019

b: Poile Sengupta is a novelist, poet, playwright and short fiction writer, for both children and adults. In 1968, she began “A Letter to You”, a humour column for the children’s magazine, Children’s World, which ran for…
f: Poile Sengupta is a novelist, poet, playwright and short fiction writer, for both children and adults. In 1968, she began “A Letter to You”, a humour column for the children’s magazine, Children’s World, which ran for nearly three decades. She has written columns for children in Deccan Herald, Bangalore, The Times of India, Bangalore, and in Midday, Mumbai. Her recent fiction for children includes Role Call and Role Call Again, 2003, Vikram and Vetal, 2005, and Vikramaditya’s Throne, 2007. She did her Masters in English from Delhi University and later studied Children’s Literature at Carleton University, Ottawa. She has taught at college and school levels, and is a well-known theatre person. She has acted in several plays and in the award-winning films The Outhouse and Shaitan. Delegate | 2017, 2018, 2019 Writing For Children | 2017

This computer engineer has written over 20 books for children, spanning the gamut from picture books to chapter books and fiction to non-fiction, covering subjects as diverse as science and economics, fantasy and philosophy. Her forte is breaking down complex concepts into simple ideas that anyone can easily relate to and understand which is why many of her books are as popular with adults as they are with children. This was lots of fun, but he soon found that writing was more than just fun – it was actually what he really wanted to do. f: Venkat Raman Singh Shyam (b.1970) belongs to the tradition of Pardhan Gond art inaugurated by the legendary Jangarh Singh Shyam, his uncle. After apprenticing with Jangarh in the 1990s, Venkat worked a range of jobs—including as house painter, screen printer and signboard artist. He also was fortunate to be guided by the pioneering Jagdish Swaminathan. Since Jangarh’s death in 2002 hi, Venkat has pursued a full-time career in art despite several hurdles. Having travelled and exhibited widely in India, the US, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Hong Kong and Europe, Venkat has been exposed to a wide range of arts practices which have influenced his sensibility. Venkat’s graphic autobiography, Finding My Way, co-authored with S. Anand, was published in 2016 to critical acclaim. Reviewing it, The Hindu said, ‘Finding My Way is an endlessly fascinating mix: part autobiography, part oral history, part ironic and playful in tone, part homage to ancestors and tradition, part graphic novel, part Kunstlerroman — and altogether a breathtaking artistic achievement.’ John Berger said, ‘It transports the reader to another time and age and space and perspective to a degree that I’ve never seen before.’ Delegate | 2023

f: Venkataraghavan is a writer, actor, and director. His non-fiction book “The Origin Story of India’s States” was published by Penguin in 2021, and his children’s books by Pratham Books. His short fiction has appeared in The Iowa Review and The Bombay Literary Magazine. He was awarded the 2023 Neev Fellowship for Children’s Book Creators, for which he is writing a novel for early adolescents set in the Madras Zoo during the Second World War. He has written, directed, produced and performed in “Brachio: The Story of a Lighthouse”, a full-length play for children based on the principles of social justice and equity, which premiered in 2023 in Bengaluru. “Brachio”, the chapter book for children, is forthcoming from HarperCollins in 2025.

f: Vera Brosgol was born in Moscow, Russia in 1984 and moved to the United States when she was five. She studied Classical Animation at Sheridan College and spent many years working in feature animation, but now she is writing and drawing books full-time. She has storyboarded for Laika on the feature films Coraline, Paranorman, The Boxtrolls, and Kubo and the Two Strings, and was Head of Story for the Academy-Award-winning Pinnochio. Her first graphic novel, Anya’s Ghost, was published in 2011 and won an Eisner Award. Her first picture book, Leave Me Alone, was published in 2016 and won a Caldecott Honor. She lives in Portland, OR with a small dog and a sourdough starter.

f: Yuyi Morales was born in Xalapa, Mexico, the city of flowers and springs. Other honors include the Americas Award, the Golden Kite Medal, the Christopher Award, the Jane Adams Award, and the Tomas Rivera Award. In 2015 she received the Caldecott Honor for her book Viva Frida.
